query: For eutectic high-entropy alloys intended for structural applications, what single intervention could simultaneously increase strength and ductility? Formulate one testable hypothesis specifying the intervention, its proposed mechanism, the expected improvement relative to an appropriate baseline, the conditions under which it should hold, prior evidence supporting it, and an experiment that could falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: A controlled low‐temperature aging treatment that induces coherent L12 nano-precipitates in the ductile FCC lamellae of an as-cast eutectic HEA (e.g., AlCoCrFeNi2.1) will simultaneously increase its yield strength and preserve its ductility by enhancing precipitation hardening without severely reducing strain accommodation.
generation.material_initial_state: An as‐cast eutectic high-entropy alloy with a lamellar microstructure composed of a ductile FCC phase and a hard B2 (or bcc) phase.
generation.intervention: Apply a low-temperature annealing (aging) treatment (for example, ~580°C for ~24 hours) after initial thermo-mechanical processing to precipitate coherent L12 nano-scale intermetallic particles within the FCC lamellae.
generation.conditions: The treatment is conducted under ambient pressure following casting and any preliminary processing steps; the alloy composition should be similar to AlCoCrFeNi2.1, where the lamellar fcc/B2 (or equivalent) microstructure is present.
generation.structural_mediator: The nucleation of coherent L12 precipitates within the FCC lamellae creates a dual-hierarchical microstructure, leading to localized back-stress effects and microcrack-arresting at lamellar boundaries.
generation.mechanism: The L12 precipitates act as effective obstacles to dislocation motion (via Orowan-type strengthening) while their coherent nature preserves interfacial integrity. This modifies the stress distribution such that the FCC phase is strengthened (yield strength increases) yet retains sufficient ductility due to improved dislocation storage and facile strain transfer across refined lamellar interfaces.
generation.predicted_outcome: Relative to the as-cast baseline (e.g., ~770 MPa yield strength with 17–18% elongation), the intervention is expected to increase yield strength by approximately 30% (e.g., raising it to around 1000–1080 MPa) while maintaining elongation within a similar range (~13–18%), thereby alleviating the typical strength–ductility trade-off.
generation.baseline: The as-cast eutectic HEA with a naturally formed lamellar fcc + B2 microstructure without any additional aging to induce L12 precipitation.
generation.boundary: The beneficial effect is anticipated only for eutectic HEAs that possess similar phase distributions and chemical compositions (e.g., AlCoCrFeNi2.1); different compositions, non-lamellar microstructures, or alternative processing histories may not exhibit the same degree of simultaneous improvement.
generation.uncertainty: The exact magnitude of strength increase and ductility retention may vary with precise aging conditions and minor compositional differences; additional experiments are necessary to determine the optimal treatment parameters and to verify that no deleterious secondary phase formation occurs.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of identical AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic HEA samples from the same casting batch. Subject one set to the low‐temperature annealing treatment (e.g., 580°C for 24 hours) to induce L12 precipitation, while keeping the other set as the untreated (as-cast) control. Characterize the microstructure using TEM/EDS and perform quasi-static tensile tests to measure yield strength and ductility.
measurements: Quantitative analysis of L12 precipitate size, volume fraction, and distribution via transmission electron microscopy (TEM) and atom-probe tomography (APT)
Tensile yield strength and ultimate tensile strength from stress–strain curves
Elongation to failure (ductility) from mechanical testing
Phase integrity and interface quality via high-resolution imaging
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the annealed samples do not exhibit a statistically significant increase (e.g., >20%) in yield strength relative to the as-cast control or if there is a marked reduction in ductility (e.g., >15% loss in elongation), then the hypothesis that the low-temperature aging intervention simultaneously enhances strength and ductility is falsified.

cited_evidence.text: Realizing improved strength–ductility synergy in eutectic alloys acting as in situ composite materials remains a challenge in conventional eutectic systems, which is why eutectic high-entropy alloys (EHEAs), a newly-emerging multi-principal-element eutectic category, may offer wider in situ composite possibilities. Here, we use an AlCoCrFeNi2.1 EHEA to engineer an ultrafine-grained duplex microstructure that deliberately inherits its composite lamellar nature by tailored thermo-mechanical processing to achieve property combinations which are not accessible to previously-reported reinforcement methodologies. The as-prepared samples exhibit hierarchically-structural heterogeneity due to phase decomposition, and the improved mechanical response during deformation is attributed to both a two-hierarchical constraint effect and a self-generated microcrack-arresting mechanism. This work provides a pathway for strengthening eutectic alloys and widens the design toolbox for high-performance materials based upon EHEAs. The present study focuses on the marginally hypo-eutectic HEA with the nominal composition of Al0.7CoCrFeNi (15 at. % Al and 21.25 at.% each of Co, Cr, Fe, Ni). While a few previous investigations on this HEA have reported a lamellar two-phase fcc/B2microstructure in this alloy, a detailed investigation of the microstructure of this alloy and its evolution during post-solidification thermo-mechanical processing forms the basis of the present study. Furthermore, the present study also investigates the influence of such heat-treatments on the mechanical behavior of this alloy under both quasi-static low strain rate tensile loading conditions, as well as dynamic strain rate compression conditions. The results clearly indicate that with suitable heat treatments the fcc phase in the lamellar two-phase microstructure is further strengthened by forming ordered L12 nano precipitates, without compromising the tensile ductility. The precipitate free channel near the interface of the B2 + bcc and fcc + L12 lamellae (refer Fig. 5) can be relatively softer as compared to the fcc + L12 regions, and consequently act as sites for high dislocation storage in the vicinity of the interfaces during deformation. Such a mechanism could also potentially rationalize the similar strain rate sensitivity observed in case of the Al0.7CoCrFeNi eutectic HEA, in the absence or in the presence of L12 precipitates within the fcc-based lamellae.

cited_evidence.text: Al0.7CoCrFeNi alloy consists of a lamellar eutectic structure of fcc and B2/bcc phases (Figure 2). The SEM microstructure from the HTA condition is shown in Figure 2a. The backscattered electron diffraction (BSED) image in Figure 2a shows a two-phase eutectic type of microstructure with a bright contrast phase and dark contrast phase organized in the lamellar arrangement. TEM was used to identify the crystal structure and the composition of the two lamellae. Figure 2b shows the selected area diffraction patterns (SADPs) from the two phases. The SADPs was taken from the bright region in the SEM image was consistently indexed to be a fcc phase aligned in [011] zone axis, while the dark region was indexed as bcc phase consisting of ordered regions. The [001]B2/bcc zone axis is shown in Figure 2 (b, lower part). The presence of extra-super lattice spots in (001) positions in the SADP from [001]B2/bcc zone axis clearly establish the ordering of this phase. The STEM results showed that the fcc phase is enriched in Co, Cr and Fe and B2/bcc phase are enriched in Al and Ni (Figure 2c) marked with yellow and white arrows respectively in the figure.
